verses.1: Having thus pondered, Narada, moving swiftly, went towards Yama's abode to narrate the events as they had transpired.
verses.2: There, Narada saw the god Yama, honored by fire, administering the fate of all beings as it was ordained for each.
verses.3: Upon seeing the great sage Narada arrive there, Yama, having properly offered him a water offering and seated him comfortably, then spoke.
verses.4: Yama asked, "O divine sage, is all well with you, and is dharma not perishing? What is the purpose of your visit, O one revered by gods and gandharvas?"
verses.5: Then, the revered sage Narada spoke these words: "Listen, I will tell you the plan, and let it be carried out."
verses.6: O King of Pitrus, this demon named Dashagriva is approaching to bring you, who are very difficult to conquer, under his control through his valor.
verses.7: O Lord, it is for this reason that I have quickly come; what will happen today to you, the wielder of the staff of punishment?
verses.8: In the meantime, from afar, they saw the demon's radiant aerial chariot approaching, shining like the rising sun.
verses.9: The mighty one, Ravana, having illuminated the entire region with the radiance of his Pushpaka chariot, then approached that place.
verses.10: The mighty-armed Dashagriva saw living beings everywhere experiencing the fruits of both their good and evil deeds.
verses.11: He also saw Yama's soldiers along with his fierce, dreadful, and terrifying attendants.
verses.12: He saw embodied beings being killed and tormented, crying out with a great cry and intent on intense wailing.
verses.13: He saw them being devoured by worms and by fierce dogs.
verses.14: He heard them uttering terrifying cries that caused distress to the ears, and saw them repeatedly being made to cross the Vaitarani river, whose waters were blood.
verses.15: Ravana saw the unrighteous being tormented repeatedly in hot sands and cut in the forest of sword-leaves.
verses.16: He also saw them in Raurava hell, in the caustic river, and on razor-sharp edges, begging for water while thirsty and hungry.
verses.17: These miserable beings appeared like corpses, emaciated, discolored, with disheveled hair, covered in dirt and mud, and were running around frantically.
verses.18: Ravana saw hundreds and thousands of such beings on his path, but he also saw others rejoicing in splendid houses with sounds of music and singing, enjoying the fruits of their own good deeds.
verses.19: Those who gave cows enjoyed milk products, givers of food enjoyed food, and givers of houses enjoyed houses, thus partaking in the fruits of their own good deeds.
verses.20: This describes beings who were adorned by beautiful women with gold, gems, and pearls.
verses.21: The very mighty-armed Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, saw other righteous beings there, shining with their own splendor.
verses.22: Then, the powerful Ravana, by his valor and force, released those who were being tormented by their own evil deeds.
verses.23: The beings released by that Rakshasa Dashagriva indeed attained unexpected and unthought-of happiness for a moment.
verses.24: When the dead were being released by the mighty Rakshasa, the guardians of the dead became very enraged and rushed towards the lord of Rakshasas.
verses.25: Then, a great tumultuous roar arose from all directions, made by the brave warriors of Yama who were charging forward.
verses.26: Hundreds of thousands of those brave warriors showered the Pushpaka chariot with spears, iron clubs, lances, maces, javelins, and other missiles.
verses.27: They quickly shattered the seats, palaces, platforms, and archways of the Pushpaka chariot, just like bees.
verses.28: Even though that divine Pushpaka aerial chariot, which was a dwelling place for gods, was being shattered in battle, it remained indestructible due to the power of Brahma.
verses.29: The army of that great-souled Yama was immeasurably vast, comprising hundreds and thousands of brave warriors leading the charge.
verses.30: Then, those great heroic ministers of Ravana, along with King Dashanana himself, fought using trees, mountains, and hundreds of palaces, as they wished and according to their strength.
verses.31: Though their limbs were smeared with blood and they were struck by all sorts of weapons, those ministers of the Rakshasa king waged a great battle.
verses.32: O mighty-armed one, those great ministers of Yama and Ravana fiercely struck each other with their weapons.
verses.33: The mighty warriors of Yama, abandoning those ministers, rushed directly towards Dashanana (Ravana) with showers of spears.
verses.34: Then, the lord of Rakshasas, Ravana, with his limbs smeared with blood and wounded by the blows, appeared on his Pushpaka chariot like a blooming Ashoka tree.
verses.35: The powerful one indeed hurled spears, maces, nooses, shaktis, javelins, arrows, pestles, stones, and trees, empowered by his missile knowledge.
verses.36: That extremely terrible shower of trees, stones, and weapons fell upon Yama's armies on the surface of the earth.
verses.37: But having pierced through all those weapons and repelled that missile, Yama's soldiers, in hundreds of thousands, struck that single terrible demon.
verses.38: And all of them, having surrounded him like dense clouds surrounding a mountain, crushed him with bhindipalas and spears until he was breathless.
verses.39: With his armor loosened, enraged, and drenched in streams of blood, he then abandoned the Pushpaka chariot and stood on the earth.
verses.40: Then, the bow-wielding Indrajit, having regained consciousness in a moment, stood enraged in battle like the god of death.
verses.41: Then, he fixed the divine Pāśupata weapon on his bow, and having told them "Stop! Stop!", he drew that bow.
verses.42: Then, Indrajit, the enemy of Indra, enraged in battle, drew his bow up to his ear and released that arrow, just as Shiva did at Tripura.
verses.43: The form of that arrow was a smokeless circle of flames, like a raging forest fire intensifying in summer, about to consume a forest.
verses.44: That arrow, wreathed in flames and followed by flesh-eating demons, once released in battle, rushed forward, turning bushes and even trees into ashes.
verses.45: Yama's armies, burnt by the enemy's power in that battle, fell down like trees consumed by a forest fire.
verses.46: Then, the demon of terrible prowess, Ravana, along with his attendants, let out a very great roar, as if shaking the earth. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकविंशः सर्गः ।। 21 ।। Thus ends the twenty-first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
